transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor (Redwood) — Ravi Kumar, Elena Park, Marcus Li (GalaxyGrid)

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate you carving out time. I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the partner program.
[00:00:08] Ravi Kumar: Yeah thanks, Maya. Ravi here. We chatted over email, keen to understand how Redwood might integrate with GalaxyGrid infra — and what a GTM partnership could look like.
[00:00:15] Liam O'Connor: Hi all, Liam, Solutions Eng. We'll cover technical fit and then talk about partner flows. Quick note, apologies in advance for any audio dropouts — gonna be on travel wifi.
[00:00:25] Elena Park: No worries.

[00:00:30] Maya Chen: Quick agenda — intro, technical compatibility (APIs, VPC/on-prem options, KMS, SOC2), capacity and pricing, pilot/bench plan, and GTM. Sound good?
[00:00:38] Marcus Li: Yep, that works. We'll also want to confirm multi-tenant isolation and performance guarantees.

[00:00:45] Liam O'Connor: Great. On the technical side Redwood exposes a consistent inference API whether you run hosted, dedicated, or private. For partners like GalaxyGrid we typically integrate at two levels: 1) infrastructure partner — provide GPU fleets where we can run Redwood Dedicated or Private control plane; 2) reseller/managed offering where GalaxyGrid can bundle Redwood as a managed inference layer.
[00:01:05] Ravi Kumar: So both resell and host are on the table. For hosting, what's the model — do we ship a container, or does Redwood manage control plane?
[00:01:12] Liam O'Connor: Depends on the model. For Private deployments you run the control plane in your VPC, with optional on-prem installers. We support customer-managed KMS, RBAC via SAML/SSO, audit logs. For Dedicated we can run in co-located cloud accounts — Redwood manages control plane but separates tenant data. In short: flexible.
[00:01:30] Elena Park: How about kernel-level optimizations? We run a mix of A100 and H100 nodes; some of our customers want quantized LLMs.
[00:01:38] Liam O'Connor: We do kernel selection and quantization profiles in the runtime; we profile models to pick optimal kernels per architecture and sequence length. There is some nuance — certain quant formats perform differently on A100 vs H100 — but we've shipped profiles for the common open models and can calibrate on your fleet.
[00:01:55] Marcus Li: Any gotchas with KV cache or long-context models? We run many chat ops with 8-12k token contexts.
[00:02:02] Liam O'Connor: We have KV cache management and prefix caching; for long contexts we recommend dedicated smaller batch sizes and we can route long-context requests to dedicated nodes to avoid tail latency. We'll want to validate with your traffic.

[00:02:15] Maya Chen: On security — SOC 2 is standard for Redwood; we also support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit log forwarding to your SIEM. For partners, we can produce an onboarding packet that includes our compliance docs, sample contracts, and a recommended network topology for VPC peering.
[00:02:33] Ravi Kumar: Good. We need to map the network topology — particularly whether we can avoid public egress for tokenized data.
[00:02:38] Liam O'Connor: Yes — Private deployments in your VPC avoid egress. For Dedicated we can set up private connectivity (VPC peering, Direct Connect equivalents). There may be a small control plane endpoint that is reachable via specific IP ranges — we document that.

[00:02:52] Elena Park: From a GTM perspective, we're interested in co-selling and a white-label/resell option. Do you run partner enablement?
[00:02:59] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We have a partner program with enablement materials, joint marketing credit for initial pilots, and partner tiering based on committed capacity. I'll include the partner packet. We also do co-branded case studies once a pilot goes production.
[00:03:10] Ravi Kumar: Pricing — are there partner discounts or committed rates for reserved capacity?
[00:03:15] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated/reserved capacity has commit-based pricing. For partners we typically provide a wholesaler rate plus enablement credits for initial pilots. Exact tiers depend on commit size; I'll attach a sample pricing sheet.

[00:03:28] Marcus Li: For the benchmark, we want a run against our Llama-3-16k-ish workload, mixed prompt/complete, avg seq len ~2k, 30k tokens/day. Can you support that?
[00:03:37] Liam O'Connor: Yep. We'll need the model artifact or the HF weights identifier, and a representative prompt set. We'll run a perf harness that measures p50/p95 latency, throughput, and cost per token. Also we'll test dedicated vs hosted paths.
[00:03:50] Elena Park: Any integration work on our side? API wrappers?
[00:03:55] Liam O'Connor: Minimal — Redwood's REST/SDK is straightforward. For Private you deploy an agent and configure routing. For Dedicated we supply routing policies and SDK keys. We can share a terraform module and helm chart for the on-prem pieces.

[00:04:10] Ravi Kumar: Ok — what about failure modes? Auto-fallback to smaller models?
[00:04:14] Maya Chen: We support smart routing and auto-fallbacks — policies can route to cheaper model variants or alternate regions when capacity is constrained. That's a big reliability win for customers.
[00:04:23] Marcus Li: Any notes on observability? We need token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route.
[00:04:28] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdowns, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and alerting. For partners we can add visibility into partner billing and per-customer dashboards.

[00:04:40] Elena Park: Are there competitive overlaps? We're evaluating NVIDIA Cloud and CoreWeave for pure infra. Why Redwood vs building our own inference stack?
[00:04:48] Maya Chen: Our value is a production-first inference runtime plus the orchestration and billing layer. Building comparable batching, KV cache, routing, and ops is non-trivial. Partnering lets GalaxyGrid upsell managed inference without first-principles rework.
[00:05:02] Ravi Kumar: Makes sense.

[00:05:05] Liam O'Connor: Next practical step I propose: 1) Marcus shares model and sample traffic; 2) we schedule a 2-hour benchmark slot with your infra team; 3) Maya sends partner packet + pricing.
[00:05:17] Marcus Li: I'll drop the model details and a 1-page traffic profile by Monday.
[00:05:21] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll aim to run the benchmark the week of the 16th.

[00:05:27] Elena Park: One more question — SLA and support levels for partner-managed customers?
[00:05:32] Maya Chen: We offer SLA-backed options for Dedicated with different tiers (99.9%/99.95%) and prioritized support for partners. I'll include the SLA doc in the packet.

[00:05:42] Ravi Kumar: Great. That answers most of our questions.

[00:05:46] Maya Chen: Okay we'll recap in an email after the call. Thanks everyone for the time.

[00:05:50] Liam O'Connor: Thanks, talk soon.

[00:05:52] Marcus Li: Thanks all.

[End of transcript]
